core_obligations: The affine statement (proof lines 14323-14341): for an etale map R -> A with R a normal domain and fraction field K separably closed, A tensor_R K is a finite product of copies of K; since A is normal the idempotents e_i lie in A, so A = product A e_i and one may assume A tensor_R K = K; flatness gives A subset K, hence A is a domain, and the same argument gives A tensor_R A subset K, so A tensor_R A -> A is bijective, which makes R -> A an open immersion by the radicial-etale criterion.

Part (1) (proof lines 14343-14358): for a separated etale f : U -> X with generic point eta and fibre f^{-1}({eta}) = {xi_i}, the affine statement shows that over an affine open U' of U with affine image, U' = coproduct of the U'_i, the sets of specialisations of xi_i, each mapping to X as an open immersion; hence U_i = closure of {xi_i} is an open and closed subscheme of U and U_i -> X is locally on the source an isomorphism, and separatedness plus the distinct-local-rings lemma makes U_i -> X injective, so each U_i -> X is an open immersion as asserted.

Part (2) (proof lines 14360-14366): follows from part (1) together with the description of the strict henselisation of O_{X,x} as the local ring at a geometric point on the etale site; the author also records a direct proof in the chapter on fundamental groups.
proof_roadmap: Prove the affine case: split A tensor_R K into copies of K, push the idempotents into A by normality, and use the radicial criterion to see that R -> A is an open immersion.
Deduce part (1) by decomposing an affine piece of U along the specialisations of the generic points of the fibre and applying the affine case to each piece, then using separatedness for injectivity.
Deduce part (2) from part (1) and the description of strict henselisations on the etale site.
difficulty_reason: The lemma characterises integral normal schemes with separably closed function field: separated etale maps split into open immersions, and every local ring is strictly henselian (statement lines 14311-14320). The proof (proof lines 14322-14366) first settles the affine case, where normality forces the idempotents of A tensor_R K to lie in A and the radicial-etale criterion turns the resulting bijectivity of A tensor_R A -> A into an open immersion; the global statement follows by decomposing an affine piece of U along the generic points of its fibre and using separatedness for injectivity, and part (2) is read off from the description of strict henselisations. H2: an explicit affine argument followed by a two-step global reduction.
